atoms.canonical_statement: The guideline is intended to assist medical professionals who evaluate living kidney donor candidates and provide care before, during, and after donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The Work Group replaced isolated single-risk-factor decisions with a comprehensive donor-candidate risk framework based on simultaneous consideration of demographic, clinical, and donation-related factors.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The Evidence Review Team searched Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library for systematic reviews, randomized trials, and observational studies indexed through September 2014, with additional evidence identified by the Work Group through January 2017.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The systematic review identified 4,530 citations; 414 met criteria for full-text review after title and abstract screening, and 70 additional references were found by supplemental citation searching, yielding 484 full-text references.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Long-term donor outcome studies had to include a healthy nondonor comparison group with similar baseline health characteristics; comparisons with the general population were not eligible.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: KDIGO used GRADE for recommendations informed by the systematic review: Level 1 denotes a strong recommendation, Level 2 a weaker recommendation, and evidence certainty is graded A through D; statements outside the eligible evidence review are reported as Not Graded.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: KDIGO collaborated with the CKD Prognosis Consortium to build a proof-of-concept model projecting 15-year and lifetime kidney-failure risk in the absence of donation from multiple demographic and health characteristics.

source_anchor.paragraph: De novo evidence generation and Chapter 1

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: A draft guideline underwent open public review in November and December 2015; the Work Group revised the document in response to public comments before all members approved the final version.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Most recommendations are ungraded because many clinically important living-donation questions were outside the systematic review or were not amenable to randomized or controlled observational study.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The guideline states that its literature searches were comprehensive but not exhaustive; hand searches of journals, review articles, and textbook chapters were not systematically performed.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The kidney-failure risk model is a proof-of-concept tool that requires validation; uncertainty is greatest for lifetime risk, younger candidates, populations outside the United States, ethnicities other than the black and white groups represented in the model, and individualized donation-attributable risk.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The donor candidate's willingness to donate a kidney voluntarily without undue pressure should be verified.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The benefits and risks of kidney donation should be assessed for each donor candidate.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The decision to accept or exclude a donor candidate should follow transplant program policies.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidate decision-making should be facilitated through education and counseling on individualized risks and benefits, methods to minimize risks, and the need for postdonation follow-up.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: For an accepted donor candidate, a plan for donation care and follow-up should be formulated to minimize risks of donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: For an excluded donor candidate, a plan for any needed care and support should be formulated.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The donor candidate, the intended recipient, and the transplant program must all agree with the decision to proceed with donation in concordance with transplant program policies and informed consent.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Transplant program policies must be defensible based on current understanding of the risks and benefits of kidney donation, and should apply to all donor candidates evaluated at the center.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Each transplant program should establish policies describing psychosocial criteria that are acceptable for donation, including any program constraints on acceptable relationships between the donor candidate and the intended recipient.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: All donor candidates should be evaluated using the same criteria, regardless of whether donation is directed towards a designated recipient.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Each transplant program should establish policies describing medical criteria that are acceptable for donation, addressing when possible, numeric thresholds for short-term and long-term postdonation risks above which the transplant program will not proceed with donation. Risks should be expressed as absolute rather than relative risks.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: When possible, transplant programs should provide each donor candidate with individualized quantitative estimates of short-term and long-term risks from donation, including recognition of associated uncertainty, in a manner that is easily understood by donor candidates.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Transplant programs should evaluate donor candidate risks in comparison to predetermined thresholds for acceptance. If a donor candidate's postdonation risk is above the transplant program's acceptable risk threshold, the risk is not acceptable for donation. If a donor candidate's postdonation risk is below the transplant program's acceptance threshold, the candidate makes the decision whether or not to proceed with donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: If a donor candidate is not acceptable, the transplant program should explain the reason for nonacceptance to the donor candidate.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Transplant programs should protect donor candidate's privacy regarding the evaluation, including all considerations in the decision to donate or not.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: A multidisciplinary transplant program team knowledgeable in kidney donation and transplantation should evaluate, care for, and formulate a plan for donor care including long-term follow-up.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Transplant programs should minimize conflict of interest by providing at least one key team member not involved in the care or evaluation of the intended recipient who evaluates the donor candidate and participates in the determination of donor acceptance.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Transplant programs should conduct as efficient a donor evaluation as possible, meeting the needs of donor candidates, intended recipients and transplant programs.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Informed consent for donation should be obtained from the donor candidate in the absence of the intended recipient, family members and other persons who could influence the donation decision.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The donor candidate's capacity to provide informed consent (ie, ability to understand the risks, benefits and consequences of donation) should be confirmed before proceeding with evaluation and donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Substitute decision makers should not be used on behalf of a donor candidate who lacks the capacity to provide informed consent (eg, children or those who are mentally challenged), except under extraordinary circumstances and only after ethical and legal review.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Protocols should be followed to provide each donor candidate with information on: • The processes of evaluation, donor acceptance, and follow-up • The types of information that may be discovered during the evaluation, and what the transplant program will do with such information • Individualized risks, benefits and expected outcomes of the donor evaluation, donation, and postdonation health, including a discussion of the uncertainty in some outcomes • Treatment alternatives available to transplant candidates, and average expected outcomes • How personal health information will be handled • Availability of transplant program personnel for support

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The donor candidate's understanding of the relevant information on the risks and benefits of donation should be confirmed before proceeding with donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates should have adequate time to consider information relevant to deciding whether they wish to donate or not.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: A donor candidate's decision to withdraw at any stage of the evaluation process should be respected and supported in a manner that protects confidentiality.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: A donor candidate who decides not to donate and has difficulty communicating that decision to the intended recipient should be assisted with this communication by the transplant program.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor ABO blood typing should be performed twice before donation to reduce the risk of unintended blood type incompatible transplantation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor blood group A subtype testing should be performed when donation is planned to recipients with anti-A antibodies.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) typing for major histocompatibility complex (MHC) Class I (A, B, C) and Class II (DP, DQ, DR) should be performed in donor candidates and their intended recipients, and donor-specific anti- HLA antibodies should be assessed in intended recipients.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates who are ABO blood group or HLA incompatible with their intended recipient should be informed of availability, risks, and benefits of treatment options, including kidney paired donation and incompatibility management strategies.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: If a donor candidate and their intended recipient are blood type or crossmatch incompatible, transplantation should be performed only with an effective incompatibility management strategy.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Nondirected donor candidates should be informed of availability, risks and benefits of participating in kidney paired donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates should receive guideline-based evaluation and management used for other noncardiac surgeries to minimize risks of perioperative complications, including a detailedhistory andexaminationtoassess risksfor cardiac, pulmonary, bleeding, anesthesia-related and other perioperative complications.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates who smoke should be advised to quit at least 4 weeks before donation to reduce their risk of perioperative complications, and commit to lifelong abstinence to prevent long-term complications.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor kidney function should be expressed as glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and not as serum creatinine concentration.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor GFR should be expressed in mL/min per 1.73 m2 rather than mL/min.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor glomerular filtration rate (GFR) should be estimated from serum creatinine (eGFRcr) for initial assessment, following recommendations from the KDIGO 2012 CKD guideline.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor GFR should be confirmed using one or more of the following measurements, depending on availability: • Measured GFR (mGFR) using an exogenous filtration marker, preferably urinary or plasma clearance of inulin, urinary or plasma clearance of iothalamate, urinary or plasma clearance of 51Cr-EDTA, urinary or plasma clearance of iohexol, or urinary clearance of 99mTc-DTPA • Measured creatinine clearance (mCrCl) • Estimated GFR from the combination of serum creatinine and cystatin C (eGFRcr-cys) following recommendations from the KDIGO 2012 CKD guideline • Repeat estimated GFR from serum creatinine (eGFRcr)

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: If there are parenchymal, vascular or urological abnormalities or asymmetry of kidney size on renal imaging, single kidney GFR should be assessed using radionuclides or contrast agents that are excreted by glomerular filtration (eg, 99mTc-DTPA).

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: GFR of 90 mL/min per 1.73 m2 or greater should be considered an acceptable level of kidney function for donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The decision to approve donor candidates with GFR 60 to 89 mL/min per 1.73 m2 should be individualized based on demographic and health profile in relation to the transplant program's acceptable risk threshold.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with GFR less than 60 mL/min per 1.73 m2 should not donate.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: When asymmetry in GFR, parenchymal abnormalities, vascular abnormalities, or urological abnormalities are present but do not preclude donation, the more severely affected kidney should be used for donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: We suggest that donor candidates be informed that the future risk of developing kidney failure necessitating treatment with dialysis or transplantation is slightly higher because of donation; however, average absolute risk in the 15 years following donation remains low. (2C)

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor proteinuria should be measured as albuminuria, not total urine protein. KDIGO Living Kidney Donor Work Group S9

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Initial evaluation of donor albuminuria (screening) should be performed using urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) in a random (untimed) urine specimen.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor albuminuria should be confirmed using: • Albumin excretion rate (AER, mg/day [mg/d]) in a timed urine specimen • Repeat ACR if AER cannot be obtained

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Urine AER less than 30 mg/d should be considered an acceptable level for donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The decision to approve donor candidates with AER 30 to 100 mg/d should be individualized based on demographic and health profile in relation to the transplant program's acceptable risk threshold.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with urine AER greater than 100 mg/d should not donate.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates should be assessed for microscopic hematuria.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with persistent microscopic hematuria should undergo testing to identify possible causes, which may include: • Urinalysis and urine culture to assess for infection • Cystoscopy and imaging to assess for urinary tract malignancy • 24-hour urine stone panel to assess for nephrolithiasis and/or microlithiasis • Kidney biopsy to assess for glomerular disease (eg, thin basement membrane nephropathy, IgA nephropathy, Alport syndrome)

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with hematuria from a reversible cause that resolves (eg, a treated infection) may be acceptable for donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with IgA nephropathy should not donate.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates should be asked about prior kidney stones, and related medical records should be reviewed if available.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The imaging performed to assess anatomy before donor nephrectomy (eg, computed tomography angiogram) should be reviewed for the presence of kidney stones.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with prior or current kidney stones should be assessed for an underlying cause.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The acceptance of a donor candidate with prior or current kidney stones should be based on an assessment of stone recurrence risk and knowledge of the possible consequences of kidney stones after donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates and donors with current or prior kidney stones should follow general population, evidencebased guidelines for the prevention of recurrent stones.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates should be asked about prior episodes of gout.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates may be informed that donation is associated with an increase in serum uric acid concentration, which may increase the risk for gout.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates and donors with prior episodes of gout should be informed of recommended methods to reduce their risk of future episodes of gout.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Blood pressure should be measured before donation on at least2occasionsbyclinicalstafftrainedinaccuratemeasurement technique, using equipment calibrated for accuracy.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: When the presence or absence of hypertension in a donor candidate is indeterminate based on history and clinic measurements (eg, blood pressure is high normal or variable), blood pressure should be further evaluated using ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) or repeated using standardizedblood pressure measurements.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Normal blood pressure, as defined by guidelines for the general population in the country or region where donation is planned, is acceptable for donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with hypertension that can be controlled to systolic blood pressure less than 140 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure less than 90 mm Hg using 1 or 2 antihypertensive agents, who do not have evidence of target organ damage, may be acceptable for donation. The decision to approve donor candidates with hypertension should be individualized based on demographic and health profile in relation to the transplant program's acceptable risk threshold.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates should be counseled on lifestyle interventions to address modifiable risk factors for hypertension and cardiovascular disease, including healthy diet, smoking abstinence, achievement of healthy body weight, and regular exercise according to guidelines for the general population. These measures should be initiated before donation and maintained lifelong.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: We suggest that donor candidates should be informed that blood pressure may rise with aging, and that donation may accelerate a rise in blood pressure and need for antihypertensive treatment over expectations with normal aging. (2D)

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Risk factors for kidney and cardiovascular disease should be identified before donation and addressed by counseling to promote long-term health.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Body mass index (BMI) should be computed based on weight and height measured before donation, and classified based on World Health Organization (WHO) criteria for the general population or race-specific categories.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The decision to approve donor candidates with obesity and BMI >30 kg/m2 should be individualized based on demographic and health profile in relation to the transplant program's acceptable risk threshold.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates who have had bariatric surgery should be assessed for risk of nephrolithiasis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates should be asked about prior diagnosis of diabetes mellitus, gestational diabetes, and family history of diabetes.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Glycemia should be assessed by fasting blood glucose and/or glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) before donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: 2-hour glucose tolerance or HbA1c testing should be performed in donor candidates with elevated fasting blood glucose, history of gestational diabetes, or family history of diabetes in a first-degree relative, and results should be used to classify diabetes or prediabetes status using established criteria for the general population.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with type 1 diabetes mellitus should not donate.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The decision to approve donor candidates with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes should be individualized based on demographic and health profile in relation to the transplant program's acceptable risk threshold.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes should be counseled that their condition may progress over time and may lead to end-organ complications.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Fasting lipid profile (including total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C and triglycerides) should be measured as part of an overall cardiovascular risk assessment before donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The decision to approve donor candidates with dyslipidemia should be individualized based on demographic and health profile in relation to the transplant program's acceptable risk threshold.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The use of tobacco products should be assessed before donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates who use tobacco products should be counseled on the risks of perioperative complications, cancer, cardio-pulmonary disease and kidney failure, should be advised to abstain from use of tobacco products, and should be referred to a tobacco cessation support program if possible.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: The decision to approve donor candidates who are active tobacco users should be individualized based on demographic and health profile in relation to the transplant program's acceptable risk threshold.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Risk for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections should be assessed before donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates should be assessed for factors associated with an increased likelihood of endemic or unexpected infections, including geographic, seasonal, occupational, animal and environmental exposures.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates should complete a urinalysis and testing for HIV, HBV, HCV, cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein- Barr virus (EBV), and Treponema pallidum (syphilis).

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: If indicated by regional epidemiology or individual history, donor candidates should complete testing for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Strongyloides, Trypanosoma cruzi, West Nile virus, Histoplasmosis, and/or Coccidiomycosis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Transplant programs should develop protocols to screen donor candidates for emerging infections in consultation with local public health specialists.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: In general, donor infection risk factor and microbiological assessments should be performed or updated as close in time to donation as possible. For HIV, HBV and HCV, screening should be current within 28 days of donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: If a donor candidate is found to have a potentially transmissible infection, then the donor candidate, intended recipient and transplant program team should weigh the risks and benefits of proceeding with donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates should undergo cancer screening consistent with clinical practice guidelines for the country or region where the donor candidate resides. Transplant programs should ensure that screening is current according to guideline criteria at the time of donation.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: In general, donor candidates with active malignancy should be excluded from donation. In some cases of active malignancy with low transmission risk, a clear management plan and minimal risk to the donor, donation may be considered.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: A kidney with a small simple (Bosniak I) cyst can be left in the donor, particularly if there are compelling reasons for donating the contralateral kidney.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donation of a kidney with a Bosniak II renal cyst should proceed only after assessment for the presence of solid components, septations, and calcifications on the preoperative computed tomography scan (or magnetic resonance imaging) to avoid accidental transplantation of a kidney with cystic renal cell carcinoma.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with high grade Bosniak renal cysts (III or higher) or small (T1a) renal cell carcinoma curable by nephrectomy may be acceptable for donation on a caseby-case basis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with a history of treated cancer that has a low risk of transmission or recurrence may be acceptable for donation on a case-by-case basis.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates should be asked about their family history of kidney disease, and when present, the type KDIGO Living Kidney Donor Work Group S11 of disease, time of onset, and extra-renal manifestations associated with the disease.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: When the intended recipient is genetically related to the donor candidate, the cause of the intended recipient's kidney failure should be determined whenever possible. The intended recipient should consent to share this medical information with the donor evaluation team, and with the donor candidate if it could affect the decision to donate.

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates found to have a genetic kidney disease that can cause kidney failure should not donate.

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates must provide informed consent for genetic testing if indicated as part of their evaluation. provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

atoms.canonical_statement: In cases where it remains uncertain whether the donor candidate has a genetic kidney disease and whether the disease can cause kidney failure, donation should proceed only after informing the donor candidate of the risks of donation if the disease manifests later in life.

atoms.canonical_statement: Donor candidates with a family history of ADPKD in a first-degree relative may be acceptable for donation if they meet age-specific imaging or genetic testing criteria that reliably exclude ADPKD.

atoms.canonical_statement: Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1) genotyping may be offered to donor candidates with sub-Saharan African ancestors. Donor candidates should be informed that having 2 APOL1 risk alleles increases the lifetime risk of kidney failure but that the precise kidney failure risk for an affected individual after donation cannot currently be quantified.

atoms.canonical_statement: Local guidelines should be followed to confirm the absence of pregnancy before performing radiologic tests, including abdominal computed tomography (with iodinated contrast) or nuclear medicine GFR testing.

atoms.canonical_statement: A decision to proceed with donation in the year after childbirth should consider the psychological needs of mother and child, and should include anesthesia and analgesia planning for nursing mothers.

atoms.canonical_statement: Women with childbearing potential should be informed of the need to avoid becoming pregnant from the time of approval for donation to the time of recovery after nephrectomy; a quantitative human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) pregnancy test should be performed and confirmed as negative immediately before donation.

atoms.canonical_statement: Women with childbearing potential who proceed with donation should be counseled on how to reduce the risk of complications in future pregnancies.
